content.title: Whirlpool Faces Credit Downgrade As Impairments Meet KBIS 2026 Push
content.summary: S&P cut Whirlpool's (NYSE:WHR) credit rating from investment grade, citing margin pressure, leverage, and tariff risk. Whirlpool recorded a sizeable goodwill and intangible asset impairment in the fourth quarter. The company plans to highlight new home appliance products at KBIS 2026. Whirlpool, which focuses on large home appliances under brands such as Whirlpool, KitchenAid, and Maytag, is facing a mix of financial strain and product investment. content.title: WHR Q4 Deep Dive: Tariffs, Housing Headwinds, and New Product Launches Shape Outlook
content.summary: Home appliances manufacturer Whirlpool (NYSE:WHR) missed Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q4 CY2025, with sales flat year on year at $4.10 billion. The company’s full-year revenue guidance of $15.45 billion at the midpoint came in 0.8% below analysts’ estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $1.10 per share was 27.6% below analysts’ consensus estimates.
